summary: Time-warps first-input channels using a single warp curve from the second input as either rate control or index control.
key_concepts: Warp CHOP time-warps the first input channels using one warp curve from the second input.
Rate Control treats 1 as unchanged speed, values above 1 as faster, values below 1 as slower, and negative values as reverse.
Index Control treats the warp curve values as direct indices into the first input.
The output channel count, channel names, and sample rate come from the pre-warp first input.
The output start/end interval comes from the warp-curve second input.
Passing a rate curve through Speed CHOP and then using Index Control is equivalent to Rate Control in many workflows.

key_params.name: rate
key_params.note: Interpret second input as playback-rate curve

key_params.name: index
key_params.note: Interpret second input as an index into first input

key_params.name: scaleindex
key_params.note: Stretch index values to the channel length

common_gotchas: Input 0 is the pre-warp channels; input 1 is a single warp curve.
Usually intended for non-time-sliced pre-keyframed motion channels.
Rate value 1 keeps normal speed, greater than 1 speeds up, less than 1 slows down, and negative rates reverse.
Index control treats the warp curve as a direct lookup into input 0.
Output channel names/count and sample rate come from input 0, but output interval comes from the warp curve input.
Passing a rate curve through Speed CHOP then using Index Control is equivalent to Rate Control in many workflows.
